title: Let’s talk money-wise for once. Have to guys made any money?
author: Icy_Masterpiece_4414
selftext:
This is a post for people who monetized their game(s).  
Whether it be through freemium methods or game cost, or Roblox server or whatever.  
So I’m referring more to people with an entrepreneurship reasoning behind making games and not (only) because of passion.

Did you manage to make some profit thanks to AI development? Did you do it all alone with AI? Did you have to promote your game a lot or did the money came more easily than expected? I’d be glad if you shared your experience!

comments.author: TheZorro1909
comments.body:
Entrepreneurship? Are you serious?
Letting AI create a cashgrab isn't entrepreneurship

replies.author: XalAtoh
replies.body:
Generating a game is little bit more valuable than generating AI art.

IF anyone can do it... it probably not a viable business strategy, thus using the word entrepeneurship is a bit overkill.

comments.author: OriginlessGamer
comments.body:
$32 gross - Steam game (13 copies sold, 103 wishlists so far), it looks very AI-ish and website-ish, casino sim  
  
$2 - an app on itch (random donation) - procedural tile generator (for pixel art)

comments.author: MadJagStudios
comments.body: No. The gaming industry needs less cash grab and more passion.

comments.author: lyeeedar
comments.body: Yes, my game makes enough that it's my full time job

comments.author: jewfro7861
comments.body:
$286 in steam revenue. About 3 weeks on market. Not actually a profit considering tooling cost and very light marketing test ($150 ish for marketing) 

36 copies sold. 4 organic positive reviews and one from a friend who was playing a very similiar game and I gave a copy too. So its not counted but they have sunk 20+ hours into it already so.

replies.author: OldLead4716
replies.body: Dose the 150 include the steam listing ?

replies.author: jewfro7861
replies.body: Naw its a mix of mailing list and paid ads

replies.author: jewfro7861
replies.body:
I also wouldn't say I set out to do this purely for economics or anything and going into this I was still much more interested in making a game I want to play (and do).

Im pouring a lot of time and energy into this and the chance of it paying back is probably small to be honest. Especially economically I have a great day job. 

Ai hasn't changed as much as people think in sone ways. There were obviously people making money off fast asset flips before all this existed, im sure some people who figured out a good marketing system and distribution channel made money but a lot failed, same things going to happen with ai. 

I wouldnt set out on this with some grand idea youll make money unless you are sitting on an idea you already know how to go to market, and if you did you probably wouldn't be asking this question. So bet on yourself or dont but youd be better of buying couches off Facebook marketplace and reselling them if you want easy enough money, not launching a soulless market less product into the void.

comments.author: Purple_Bathroom
comments.body: getting there, but first need to make game visible.

comments.author: bingewavecinema
comments.body: Yes, I've made money on pre-orders for my game and I have about 1k wishlist 1 month after my Steam page was put up. So I expect some decent sales at launch.

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body: I'm not using it to make a quick profit.

comments.author: kytheon
comments.body: Yes but I made money with games before AI. So the pipeline is there. Putting slop on steam is a waste of time.

comments.author: Dicethrower
comments.body: AI driven gamedev hasn't been viable until like a month ago when opus 5.5 came out. People who aren't producing slop are still working on their games.

replies.author: Codingology
replies.body: I completely agree. Is taking me far much time compared to other people to make a simple game app, but I don't want to just give a prompt and let AI do everything. If you don't put your human touch into the UI, modeling, animation and textures you hardly will succeed in my opinion

replies.author: nickater
replies.body: Lógico, un buen juego lleva tiempo, el mío me llevo como 6 meses de trabajo, y no lo saqué hasta que estuve orgulloso del resultado y todavía no lo termino hay mucho que me falta por hacer.

comments.author: nickater
comments.body: Estoy recién empezando con mi primer juego serio (hice uno antes como experimento), pero ya a habido gente que a comprado el paquete de pago, llevo unos 6 dólares de ganancia jaja (es poco,lo sé, pero apenas tengo 30 descargas). Estoy considerando invertir en Google ads, pero me da miedo no recuperar la inversión.

comments.author: geddy
comments.body: You approach any hobby with the intention of making money and you’re going to have a bad time.

replies.author: Icy_Masterpiece_4414
replies.body: your hobby is making AI games? I understand making the games by yourself, writing the code, modeling etc, but prompting AI to do it is your hobby?

replies.author: Purple-Income-4598
replies.body: designing the mechanics, world, narrative... or are all games to you just quick 15 minute incremental prototypes?

replies.author: NSTStudios
replies.body: "Prompting AI" is so reductive. If someone hires a developer to build a game idea they care about, would that be just "prompting coders"? I think there are a lot of vibe coders out there that experience creating a game, refining it over time for it to just not feel like "prompting AI".

replies.author: Former-Storm-5087
replies.body: I would argue that hiring someone to do my hobby for me kinda defeats the purpose
